sc_if_runs_true.title: When does an if block run?
sc_if_runs_true.prompt: In Python, when does the indented code under `if condition:` run?
sc_if_runs_true.hint: Python evaluates the condition before entering the indented block.

help.concept: An `if` block runs only when its condition evaluates to `True`.
help.hint_1: A false condition causes Python to skip that block.
help.hint_2: Choose the option that says the block runs for the true case.

options.b: It runs only when the condition is True
options.c: It runs only when the condition is False
options.d: It runs only when there is an else block

sc_elif_role.title: What is elif for?
sc_elif_role.prompt: What is the main purpose of `elif` in Python?
sc_elif_role.hint: `elif` is checked only after earlier conditions in the same chain were false.

help.concept: `elif` adds another condition to the same conditional chain.
help.hint_2: It gives Python another condition to test before an optional `else`.

options.a: To repeat the same block many times
options.b: To check another condition if earlier ones were false
options.d: To print the value of a variable

mc_valid_conditional_facts.title: Facts about conditional chains
mc_valid_conditional_facts.prompt: Choose all true statements about `if` / `elif` / `else` chains in Python.
mc_valid_conditional_facts.hint: Think about one conditional chain, not separate independent `if` statements.

help.concept: A single `if`/`elif`/`else` chain is checked from top to bottom and runs only its first matching branch.
help.hint_1: `else` is the fallback when no earlier condition matched.
help.hint_2: Python does not continue through the same chain after a branch has been selected.

options.a: Python checks the conditions from top to bottom
options.b: More than one branch in the same chain can run for one input
options.c: Python stops after the first true branch in the chain
options.d: The else block runs when earlier conditions were false

mc_truthy_values.title: Facts about if and else
mc_truthy_values.prompt: Which statements about an `if` / `else` pair are true? Choose all that apply.
mc_truthy_values.hint: An `if` / `else` pair represents two alternative paths.

help.concept: The `if` block handles the true case; `else` handles the remaining case.
help.hint_1: `else` has no condition of its own.
help.hint_2: For one `if` / `else` pair, exactly one branch runs.

options.b: Both branches run for the same input
options.d: `else` can appear by itself without a preceding `if`

sketch_if_basic.title: Run one block with if
sketch_if_basic.bodyMarkdown:
An `if` statement runs its indented block only when its condition is `True`.

```python
temperature = 30

if temperature > 25:
    print("warm")
```

Output:

```text
warm
```

Python evaluates `temperature > 25` first. Because the comparison is `True`, the indented `print(...)` runs.

If the condition is `False`, Python skips the block:

```python
temperature = 18

if temperature > 25:
    print("warm")
```

This program prints nothing.

The basic shape is:

```python
if condition:
    # runs only when condition is True
```

The colon starts the block, and the indented lines belong to that `if`.

sketch_if_else.title: Choose between two paths with else
sketch_if_else.bodyMarkdown:
Add `else` when exactly one of two paths should run.

```python
score = 72

if score >= 60:
    print("pass")
else:
    print("fail")
```

If `score >= 60` is `True`, Python runs the `if` block and skips the `else` block.

If the condition is `False`, Python skips the `if` block and runs `else`.

So:

- `72` prints `pass`;
- `40` prints `fail`.

An `else` branch does not have its own condition. It handles every case not taken by the preceding `if`.
